new_scholarship.name: Aalborg University Master's Programme Scholarships for Non-EU/EEA Applicants
new_scholarship.description: Aalborg University grants a limited number of scholarships - approximately 15 each year - to individually selected non-EU/EEA applicants for its master's programmes, for the September intake. The scholarships are financed by the Danish Government and awarded by Aalborg University, and there is no separate scholarship application: all non-EU/EEA applicants are automatically considered when they apply to a master's programme. Each scholarship consists of a tuition fee waiver plus a monthly stipend paid across the four semesters of the master's programme.
new_scholarship.duration: Four semesters (two years), the standard duration of a master's degree at Aalborg University
new_scholarship.deadline: There is no separate scholarship application; non-EU/EEA applicants are considered automatically with their master's programme application. Aalborg University's published application deadlines for master's applicants are: September intake - 15 January 23:59 CET for fee-paying applicants, 1 March 23:59 CET for non-fee-paying applicants; February intake - 15 October 23:59 CET for all applicants.
new_scholarship.application_period: September intake: fee-paying (non-EU/EEA) applicants 15 January 23:59 CET, non-fee-paying applicants 1 March 23:59 CET; February intake: 15 October 23:59 CET for all applicants
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants from outside the EU/EEA applying to a master's programme at Aalborg University are automatically considered; EU/EEA students cannot apply for scholarships at AAU. Selection is based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications.
eligibility: Applicant must hold citizenship of a country outside the EU/EEA (EU/EEA students cannot apply for scholarships at AAU)
Applicant must be admitted to, or applying to, a master's programme at Aalborg University for the September intake

new_scholarship.name: RESDOC - Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project (MSCA COFUND Doctoral Researcher Positions, University of Helsinki)
legacy_titles: University of Helsinki RESDOC Doctoral Researcher Positions 2026 (30 Fully Funded PhD Positions)
new_scholarship.description: RESDOC (Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project) is an international doctoral training project at the University of Helsinki that runs from 2027 to 2031 and recruits 30 doctoral researchers on full-time employment contracts. It is funded under the EU MSCA COFUND programme and covers four interdisciplinary themes: infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance, biodiversity and nature's resilience, secure and sustainable food and water systems, and just socio-ecological transition. The 2026 call closed on 31 August 2026 with 2,159 applications, of which 1,023 (47%) were found eligible, and the evaluation stage was still in progress as of 2026-10-04.
new_scholarship.duration: Four years full-time, with residence in Finland for the full duration
new_scholarship.deadline: The 2026 RESDOC call closed on 31 August 2026 at 11:59 PM Finnish time (EET); applications had to be submitted by that deadline. As of 2026-10-04 the call is closed and evaluation is under way, with the written-application evaluation to be finalised by mid-October 2026 and interview rounds in late October 2026.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a completed master's degree qualifying for doctoral studies, must not hold a PhD, must be an early-stage researcher with less than four years of full-time-equivalent research experience, must fulfil University of Helsinki English language requirements, must not be permanently employed by the University, must comply with the MSCA mobility rule, must be willing to reside in Finland for the full four years, and must propose a research topic fitting the RESDOC themes.
eligibility: Master's degree or equivalent qualifying for doctoral studies, fully completed and dated in the certificate by the call deadline of 31 August 2026
Must not hold a doctoral (PhD) degree
Early-stage researcher: less than four years of full-time-equivalent research experience after the master's degree
English language requirements of the University of Helsinki met; applications submitted in English
Not permanently employed by the University of Helsinki
MSCA mobility rule: no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in Finland between 1 September 2023 and the call deadline
Willing to reside in Finland for the full four-year duration of the project
Research topic must fit the RESDOC themes and available supervision
coverage: Full-time salaried employment contract with the University of Helsinki for the doctoral research period
No tuition fees are collected from doctoral researchers at the University of Helsinki
benefits: Fully funded doctoral degree through a 100% employment contract with the University of Helsinki
Salary and social security as a University employee, including occupational health care
Doctoral tuition is free at the University of Helsinki
Participation in the RESDOC doctoral training programme across four interdisciplinary themes
required_documents: Europass CV in the predefined Europass template
Letter of Motivation in the predefined RESDOC template
Research proposal, ethics self-assessment and intersectoral mobility plan in the predefined RESDOC template
Scanned degree certificate and transcript of records (with official translations where applicable)
Proof of English language skills (optional at application, mandatory for selected candidates by 31 December 2026)
new_scholarship.english_requirement: Applicants must meet the University of Helsinki English language requirements. Proficiency can be stated but need not be proven at the application stage; selected candidates must provide valid proof by 31 December 2026.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Two-stage evaluation with a threshold grade of 3 per criterion. The written application carries 70% weight and the interview 30%. Written criteria are thematic fit, quality and novelty of the research plan, feasibility of the workplan, study and intersectoral mobility plan, and applicant competence.

new_scholarship.best_fit: Recent master's graduates with under four years of research experience who want a funded four-year PhD at the University of Helsinki on sustainability, biodiversity, food/water or socio-ecological transition themes

new_scholarship.degree_level_confirmed: RESDOC 'offers a unique opportunity to complete a fully funded doctoral degree at the University of Helsinki in Finland' and positions are salaried doctoral researcher posts in the University's doctoral programmes, with a master's degree required for eligibility.

new_scholarship.description: The University of Helsinki Doctoral School funds salaried doctoral researcher positions across the University's doctoral programmes, with one application period each year. The positions are designated as full-time work and aim for the doctoral researcher to complete a post-graduate doctoral degree within four years. The 2026 application period was 24 August to 7 September 2026 and has closed. The University does not collect tuition fees from doctoral researchers.

new_scholarship.description: The University of Oulu collects tuition fees from non-EU/EEA students admitted to English-taught Bachelor's and Master's degree programmes, and offers two partial reductions: an Early Bird discount on the first-year fee and Tuition Fee Waiver Scholarships from the second year onwards. The Early Bird discount is granted if the tuition fee is paid within three weeks of the admission results being published, and the Tuition Fee Waiver Scholarship requires at least 60 ECTS credits completed in the preceding academic year. Both reductions are percentage-based, vary by degree programme, and no University of Oulu scholarship covers 100% of the tuition fee.
new_scholarship.duration: Full degree programme; the Early Bird discount covers the first academic year and Tuition Fee Waiver Scholarships apply from the second year onwards
new_scholarship.deadline: The Early Bird discount is granted 'if the tuition fee is paid within three weeks of the admission results being published'. For programmes where the Early Bird discount is not available, or if the full fee is paid instead, the fee must be paid by the deadline given in the admission offer, and the University directs applicants to check the programme's application timeline and deadlines for the exact payment deadline.
new_scholarship.application_period: Admission to the autumn 2027 intake; the Early Bird payment window opens when admission results are published and closes three weeks later
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Tuition fee liability applies to students admitted to English-taught Bachelor's and Master's programmes who are not EU/EEA or Swiss citizens and do not hold an exempting Finnish residence permit. Early Bird discounts are available for selected programmes, and Tuition Fee Waiver Scholarships from the second year onwards require at least 60 ECTS credits completed in the preceding academic year in accordance with the approved study plan, including the required Finnish language studies.

Exempt if holding a residence permit based on temporary protection, an EU Blue Card in Finland, or right of residence under the withdrawal agreement (Brexit residence permit)
Exempt with a continuous (type A) residence permit granted on the basis of employment where the applicant's first Finnish residence permit was not granted on the basis of studies
Exempt with a continuous (type A) residence permit based on family ties where the family member's first residence permit was not granted on the basis of studies
